# agent-conversation-memory

> Bounded conversation memory for LLM agents — token-budget rolling window, pinned messages, evicted-history recall.

agent-conversation-memory keeps an agent's conversation within a token
budget without dropping the system prompt or losing evicted facts
silently. Messages are added via `addMessage`; the active window evicts
the oldest **non-pinned** messages (in insertion order) whenever total
estimated tokens exceed `tokenBudget` — pinned messages (e.g. the system
prompt) are never evicted. An `onEvict` callback fires for each evicted
message, enabling the summarize-and-reinsert pattern: you supply your own
summarizer function and call `addMessage` again with the summary — this
library makes no LLM calls itself. Evicted messages stay searchable via a
keyword inverted index (`recall(keyword)`), and the full state
round-trips through `exportJSON`/`importJSON`. Token estimation defaults
to a built-in chars/4 heuristic but accepts any custom estimator. Zero
runtime dependencies, strict TypeScript.

## API

- `class ConversationMemory(options: ConversationMemoryOptions)`
  - `addMessage(input: AddMessageInput): Message`
  - `getMessages(): Message[]` — current active window
  - `getEvicted(): Message[]` — all evicted messages, in eviction order
  - `recall(keyword: string): RecallResult[]` — keyword search over evicted history
  - `activeTokens(): number`
  - `exportJSON(): string`
  - `importJSON(json: string): void`
- `defaultEstimateTokens(text: string): number` — the built-in chars/4 estimator
- Types: `Message { id, role, content, pinned?, timestamp? }`, `AddMessageInput`, `TokenEstimator`, `EvictionCallback`, `ConversationMemoryOptions { tokenBudget, estimateTokens?, onEvict? }`, `RecallResult { message, matchedKeywords }`

## Install

```
npm install agent-conversation-memory
```

Part of the Ferrow open-source toolkit: https://github.com/Ruzylo-cloud/ferrow-toolkit — sponsored by https://ferrow.ai
